newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Clabecq union cool on social plan.
newsitem.headline: Clabecq union cool on social plan.

text.p: The union leader at bankrupt Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq on Wednesday poured cold water on a social plan for the firm's 1,800 workers put forward by the regional government, saying it offered no guarantees.

Roberto D'Orazio, spokesman for the socialist FGTB union at Clabecq, was quoted by Belgian media as saying on Wednesday the plan was "peppered with traps" and unacceptable because the government has said it must be accepted without discussion.
"We want to know what real guarantees we have, what chances we have (with) a takeover," D'Orazio added on Belgian television.
The Walloon Region, Clabecq's majority shareholder, put forward the package on Monday following talks with unions, Clabecq's court-appointed receivers and federal ministers.
The plan aims to alleviate the consequences of bankruptcy for the workers and create conditions for the company's activities to be taken over.
Among other things it covers early retirement, the problem of workers over 50, and the allocation of money made on the sale of stock.

Walloon region officials and Clabecq's receivers have been trying since it went bankrupt in January to find a buyer for the company, which suffered from high costs, poor margins and low-quality products.
Last week Italian-based private steel and commodities trading group Duferco was named as an interested candidate.
